structure.overview: The case concerns the Applicants' judicial review of the Refugee Appeal Division's (RAD) decision upholding the Refugee Protection Division's (RPD) finding that they are not Convention refugees or in need of protection and that a viable internal flight alternative (IFA) exists. The Applicants argued errors in credibility findings, procedural fairness, IFA assessment, and rejection of new evidence. The Federal Court dismissed the application, finding no procedural fairness breach, no error in rejecting new evidence, and that the RAD's credibility and IFA assessments were reasonable despite minor inconsistencies.

party_points.text: RAD erred on credibility, procedural fairness, IFA assessment, and new evidence acceptance
RAD made unreasonable factual findings, ignored corroborative evidence, overlooked contradictory medical report
RAD erred by relying on minor inconsistencies, overzealous scrutiny, unreasonable inferences in credibility
RAD erred in IFA assessment by relying on Principal Applicant's credibility finding
RAD unreasonably rejected new evidence, failed to consider subsection 110(4) properly
RAD's credibility findings reasonable based on inconsistencies
RAD reasonably rejected evidence available at RPD hearing due to inconsistencies
RAD did not raise new issues on appeal

summaries.speaker: below

summaries.summary: RAD rejected most new evidence as reasonably available before RPD hearing, accepting only affidavits about CJNG operations.

citations.cite: subsection 110(4) of the Act

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: RAD noted no oral hearing requested and limited jurisdiction to hold one only if new evidence raises serious credibility issue central to decision, which was not met.

summaries.speaker: below

Principal Applicant's abduction testimony not credible

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: RAD found most significant inconsistency was no mention in BOC of increasing extortion amount, central to oral testimony, a finding RPD did not make.

summaries.speaker: below

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court frames two issues: whether RAD breached procedural fairness by making credibility findings without oral hearing, and whether Decision is reasonable.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court agrees standard of review on merits is reasonableness as per Supreme Court's Vavilov decision.

citations.cite: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 [Vavilov]
citations.why: Establishes reasonableness standard of review

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Reasonableness is deferential but robust; courts must defer to decision-maker's expertise and avoid reweighing evidence absent exceptional circumstances.

citations.cite: Vavilov at paras 12–13, 93, 125
citations.why: Explains reasonableness standard and deference to decision-maker

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Reasonableness review requires assessing if decision is coherent, rational, and justified by facts and law, with higher burden when rights are severely affected.
idea_list: Higher burden when rights severely affected

citations.cite: Vavilov at paras 13, 85, 100, 133
citations.why: Sets criteria for reasonableness review and burden

citations.cite: Mason v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2023 SCC 21 at para 76
citations.why: Confirms increased burden when rights impacted

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Reasons are primary to show reasonableness but need not be perfect or respond to every argument.

citations.cite: Vavilov at paras 81, 91, 104, 128
citations.why: Explains reasonableness and reasons requirements

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: To find unreasonableness, flaws must be central or significant, not minor or peripheral errors.

citations.cite: Vavilov at para 100
citations.why: Defines threshold for unreasonableness

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Subsection 110(3) of the Act requires RAD to proceed without hearing, relying on RPD record and documentary evidence, with exceptions.

citations.cite: Subsection 110(3) of the Act
citations.why: Sets RAD's paper-based appeal procedure

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Subsection 110(6) allows RAD to hold hearing only if new documentary evidence raises serious credibility issue, is central, and determinative.

citations.cite: Subsection 110(6) of the Act
citations.why: Defines conditions for RAD oral hearing

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court held RAD must provide notice and opportunity to respond if it raises new issues not raised on appeal, citing Ching.

citations.cite: Ching v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2015 FC 725 at para 71
citations.why: Establishes RAD's duty to notify on new issues

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: If new evidence meets criteria, RAD must assess admissibility for credibility, relevance, and newness, citing Singh.

citations.cite: Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Singh, 2016 FCA 96 at para 49
citations.why: Explains RAD's assessment of new evidence admissibility

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Respondent made no submissions except that RAD did not raise new issues on appeal.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court finds RAD did not breach procedural fairness by not holding oral hearing as Applicants did not request one and new evidence did not meet threshold.

citations.cite: subsection 110(6) of the Act

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court agrees RAD's additional credibility findings were not new issues requiring response opportunity, distinguishing from Abraha case.
idea_list: RAD's credibility findings not new issues

citations.cite: Abraha

summaries.summary: Adverse credibility findings were not necessarily determinative of the Decision.
